dedupe_keys.name: port of london authority climate change adaptation report second round update 2015

description: The Port of London Authority (PLA), the statutory harbour authority for the tidal River Thames, sent this adaptation update to the Secretary of State in December 2015 under the voluntary second round of the UK Climate Change Act adaptation reporting, reviewing its first report to Defra in 2011. Coverage: the tidal Thames from Teddington to the outer estuary, with commercial shipping, passenger boats and heavy recreational use. Findings: most 2011 actions had been completed; the 2013-14 winter showed record fluvial flows from the non-tidal river; the Thames Barrier is being closed more often, mainly for fluvial events, and the PLA is assessing with the Environment Agency what more frequent closures mean for river trade; hot spells raise recreational incidents; lower depths and faster winter flows affect the upper reaches; coastal squeeze threatens habitats. A new action reviews contingency for an east coast surge that coincides with stormy weather, and data sharing with the Environment Agency on flow levels was strengthened. Format and access: a 48-page PDF on GOV.UK, with annexes on UKCP09 assumptions and evaluation matrices. Licence and cost: free; no licence stated. Caveats: self-assessed risks with no quantified losses. It shows how a port authority tracks thresholds and actions for climate adaptation and hazard exposure planning. It relates to the Heathrow and Ofcom adaptation reports in the catalogue.
